intro: Meet Veyl: a compact model that finds private information in text, right on your device.
Veyl is trained on the following dataset: Veyl uses NVIDIA’s Nemotron dataset for base training. Age tuning also uses the one million example dataset from A I four Privacy.
The dataset marks where private informat: Training starts with labeled text. Here, John begins a person entity, and Smith continues it. The other words are outside the entity. These labels teach the model where a private span starts and ends.
First, the teacher learns the correct to: First, a pretrained Bert teacher learns to predict the dataset labels. Its prediction is compared with the correct answer, and training adjusts the weights to reduce that error.
Both models read the same tokens. The te: Next comes distillation. The teacher and the smaller Veyl student read the same tokens. The teacher stays frozen, while the student has six narrower layers and two attention heads.
Veyl learns from dataset labels and teac: The student gets two learning signals: the correct dataset label, and the teacher’s softer scores across possible labels. A combined loss brings both signals together.
Veyl updates its weights using both sign: Only the student updates its weights. Over training, its scores move toward the target, learning from both the labels and the teacher. The scores shown here are illustrative.
The AGE head can relabel O tokens. Exist: A small age head adds just two hundred and fifty eight parameters. It can change an outside token into an age prediction. Existing entity predictions pass through unchanged.
Every token gets a 128-dimensional vecto: Now follow inference. Every token becomes a vector with one hundred and twenty eight dimensions, combining token, position, and segment embeddings.
Each token produces a query, a key and a: Inside attention, each token produces a query, a key, and a value. The query asks what to match. The key helps make that match. The value carries information to share.
John's query scores each key. Softmax tu: John’s query is compared with every key. Softmax converts these scores into weights that add up to one. This chart shows one head in the first layer.
These weights scale value vectors. Their: Each weight scales its corresponding value vector. Adding these weighted vectors gives a context vector for John, bringing information from across the sentence into that token.
Two heads combine 64 dimensions each int: Two heads do this in parallel. Each produces sixty four dimensions. Their outputs are joined into one hundred and twenty eight dimensions, then passed through an output projection.
Each BERT layer combines attention, a fe: Each Bert layer combines attention with a feed forward network. Residual connections carry earlier information forward, and normalization stabilizes the representation. The network expands the vector, then brings it back to its original width.
The process repeats through all six layers. Each layer updates every token vector using the surrounding context. These changing vectors come from the retained floating point checkpoint for this example.
BIO labels merge into spans for redactio: A classifier scores fifty seven token labels. Here, John starts a person entity and Smith continues it. The neighboring predictions merge into one person span, ready for redaction.
Finally, quantization reduces storage while keeping the same five point one seven million parameters. The retained floating point files total about twenty point seven megabytes. The exported model is just five point four three megabytes.
Measured masking scores use different ru: On the local English masking benchmark, the two paths reach the scores shown here. They use different runtimes and tokenizers, so the difference does not isolate the effect of quantization.
outro: That is Veyl. A compact model for finding private information, with inference that can run on your device.
